chunks: I seek Thy succour against the Quraysh and those who are assisting them, because they are denying me (the rights of) kinship, have lowered my high position, and are united in opposing me in the matter (of the caliphate) which is my right, and then they said, 'Know that the rightful thing is that you have it and also that you may leave it.'

key_terms.أَمْراً هُوَ لِي: A matter that is my right

ai.seo_question: What are the key grievances Imam Ali cites in his supplication against the Quraysh?
ai.summary: This supplication, often cited in the context of the post-Umar succession debates, highlights Imam Ali’s grievance against the Quraysh for usurping his designated authority through political maneuvering rather than divine decree. It underscores the Shia perspective that the caliphs' claim to legitimacy was based on arbitrary selection ('taking or leaving') rather than the explicit right of the Ahl al-Bayt, framing the conflict as a breach of kinship and justice.
